subject: Ticket 85: external-contract module - SPLIT INTO 4 REVIEWABLE CHUNKS
description:
HIGH PRIORITY per Arnon. Was estimated 8h - an outlier, so decomposed per the standing rule that a high estimate is a design problem regardless of accuracy. Agent time is cheap; Arnon's review time is scarce, and a large diff cannot be reviewed well.

FOUR INDEPENDENTLY COMMITTABLE CHUNKS, ~2h each:

1. Create toolguard/claude_code_contract.py as a stdlib-only LEAF (needs a .pyscn.toml layer entry - completeness is enforced, so --layers goes red until it has one) and move the WIRE PROTOCOL constants: payload field names (tool_name, tool_input, hook_event_name, session_id, cwd, transcript_path), response field names (hookSpecificOutput, hookEventName, permissionDecision, permissionDecisionReason, additionalContext), event names (PreToolUse, SessionStart). Measured: 45 bare literals across 6 package modules.

2. Move the NATIVE-SEMANTICS facts with dated citations: STRIPPED_WRAPPERS (timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob, bare xargs) AND the explicitly-not-stripped list (sudo, env, npx, docker exec, ...), the word-boundary rule, ':*' equivalence, colon-is-literal mid-pattern, known-safe assignment stripping and its allow/deny asymmetry. Every entry carries doc URL, section anchor, VERIFIED date.

3. The --contract checker in tools/architecture_fitness.py. NEW INSTRUMENT, so anti-vacuity applies in full: validate against a deliberately planted bare contract literal before believing a green result. State its limit in the output - it finds KNOWN keys that escaped the module, and cannot find a field Claude Code added that we have never heard of.

4. Architecture-doc section + external-contract.mmd/.png diagram. Write what is NOT re-derivable from the code: why a separate module rather than constants.py (these facts are not ours, change without a commit here, and are correct only as of a date); why create_hook_output STAYED OUT (naive SRP argues for moving it; the argument against is that which RuntimeVerdict fields reach the wire is toolguard policy); what the import edge buys and what it does not.

BOUNDARY RULE, per function not per module: a stand-alone function whose SOLE purpose is the external contract MOVES; one referencing contract structures while carrying toolguard-specific logic STAYS and imports the names. Test: could this have been written by someone who read Claude Code's docs and knew nothing about toolguard?

Drift detection is the WEAK option per Arnon: dated constants + periodic review, NO version-pinned test.

Decide the ~696 test literals separately - a literal in a wire-level test arguably PINS the contract rather than duplicating it.
